body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: e15b633edd4c17ca7aa8b2e463568af5a99b9c04 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

This PR relaxes a fixture collision check, so I reviewed it against one question: can a box the real tool stack touches now pass as clear? I found no way it can. A box is cleared only when the capsule hits it AND GJK proves a separating plane between the box and an enclosure that still contains the whole swept band. That proof uses exact support mappings, and any doubt answers "hit".

### What looks good
- `flat_band_clear` (`crates/sim/src/verify/posed_steel.rs:271-293`) can only clear a box the capsule hit (`:208`, `capsule_hits(..) && !flat_band_clear(..)`). Every verdict that was clear before is still clear by the same arithmetic, and only capsule hits can change.
- The enclosure is right. The tip chord is swept exactly. The cylinder sits about the midpoint pose. The ball pad is `bulge + swing * hypot(max|lo|,|hi|, r)`, which uses the rim's arm, longer than the capsule's centreline arm `|hi|`. Under a rotary the growth is `dth * (rho_max over the parallelogram corners + r + pad)`; distance to a line is convex, so the corner maximum holds. `swing` is midpose's proven bound for every pose inside the interval, not just the two ends.
- `band_clear_of_box` (`crates/sim/src/fixture_mesh/mod.rs`) reuses the mesh law's `SweptBand`/`Boxed` supports and `gjk::separated`. The proof is the supporting-hyperplane bound `v.w/|v| > margin`. Contact, overlap, an exhausted search, a zero axis or a non-finite number anywhere answers "not proven", so the capsule's hit stands. There is no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests.
- The flute band is a flat cylinder from the tip up to the flute length at the tool radius. A ball or bull end lies inside it, so the tip band stays conservative.
- Scope is only the fixture box laws: (c2)/(d2) in `laws.rs`, fixed steel under a rotary in `workholding.rs`, and the spindle-C fixed reading in `c_steel.rs`. No part, stock or rapid-vs-stock law reads it. No golden, snapshot or existing test expectation changed.
- Provenance is updated (GJK 1988 / van den Bergen 1999 / Ericson). `posed_steel.rs` is 368 lines. A decisions file is included, the body has a `Changelog:` line and ends `Fixes #1305`, and the commit subjects are conventional.

### Local results (trial-merged with main `890de463`, clean merge)
| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-sim` lib | 100 passed (the 6 new `posed_steel_tests` among them) |
| sim suites (20, from `cargo xtask gate quick` plan, incl. `posed_band_cylinder` 3/3, `posed_fixture_midpose` 3/3, `posed_rapids` 5/5, `midmove_pose` 5/5, `overhang_laws` 13/13, `coarse_collision` 5/5, `fixture_mesh_posed` 9/9 +1 ignored, `fixture_stack_span` 8/8, `c_axis_fixture` 8/8) | all green |
| app suites (46 from the plan: `fixtures`, `fixture_mesh`, `fixture_mesh_posed`, `rotary_fixtures`, `rotary_verify`, `tilt`, `self_centering_vise_tilted`, `c_axis_fixture`, `verify`, ...) | 377 passed, 0 failed, 11 ignored |
| motion `real_tip` / `solid_law` | 3/3, 6/6 |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Reviewer probes (local only, not pushed), each checked against brute-force sampling of the true band
- **Cylinder vs box, random:** 6000 cases, with any axis direction, zero and moving chords, r = 0, near-zero length bands, paper-thin boxes and margins 0-0.5. 5485 were proven clear and **0 were proven clear while the sampled true band came within the margin**. The tightest proven-clear case was 0.014 mm past its margin. One case was left unproven while the sampled band stood more than 0.05 mm off: conservative.
- **Hand-built cases**, all as expected:
  - a box wholly inside the cylinder: not cleared;
  - a thin box just inside the end face near the axis: not cleared;
  - a box corner entering the side near the end face (radial 14.99 of r 15): hit; at radial 15.03: clear;
  - a box top under the end face at 0.02 mm: clear; at 0.005 mm (inside the tolerance): hit;
  - the lowest rim point of a tilted band over a box edge, at leans of 0.5, 2, 10, 45 and 80 degrees: clear at 0.02 below; hit at 0.005 below, at grazing contact and when overlapping;
  - zero axis, NaN radius or margin: not proven.
- **Whole sweep vs the true band:** a stepped stack (flute r3, shank r5, holder r15, so it has shoulders), straight moves with constant and swinging poses, in the path frame and the machine frame under a rotary. I sampled 201 instants per move, each band's rims, end faces and side. Across 5500 moves (704 swept clear, many within 0.015-0.1 mm), **0 were swept clear while the true band touched the box**. The joint between bands is covered: the holder band's bottom face is a full r 15 disc, so the shoulder annulus is steel in the model, and each band is judged on its own.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Notes (not blocking)
1. In the path frame the issue's evidence case is still convicted end to end by `stack_span::band_struck` (the column half, #1303), as the body says. `Fixes #1305` is right for the posed sweep, but a user sees the false conviction go away only when #1303 lands too. Worth one line on #1305 when it closes.
2. I did not probe arc moves. The arc's bulge rides the pad exactly as it rode the capsule's `travel` growth and the mesh law's pad, so the arc reading is unchanged from main. The `--ignored` release lanes were not run.
3. The broad phase stays the capsule and GJK runs only for boxes it hits, so runtime should not move much. I did not measure it.

Thank you for the careful enclosure write-up in the module header and the decisions file - it made checking the geometry straightforward.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
